correctness.rationale: On the branch open at b, the exponential lies below the chord from (b,0) to (1,c), which is strictly below the diagonal even at its endpoints. At b the sine branch gives 1, and at 0 it gives a>0. On [0,b), divide F(x)-x by cos²(kx) to get a-A_b(x), where A_b=x-(1-x)tan²(kx). Its derivative has the sign of 1-2kE_b(x), with E_b=(1-x)tan(kx). The numerator of E_b' is k(1-b)+u-sin(2u)/2>0, u=π/2-kx, so E_b runs from 0 to infinity. At b/2 it is 1-b/2>b/π. Hence A_b has exactly one maximum x_*<b/2; it starts at 0, rises to a_*>0, and ends at minus infinity. Also A_b(x)≤x<b, so a_*<b. This proves the 2/1/0 census. At a root F'-1=-cos²(kx)A_b', and F'>0 in the interior, giving the two multipliers. The double root has positive second derivative 2(1-a_*)k²cos(2kx_*); the increasing map with positive displacement on each side attracts locally from the left and repels on the right. Dividing the Taylor expansion by the coefficient of z² gives z²=K(b)²δ+O(δ^(3/2)) (the nondegenerate maximum first gives z=O(√δ)), yielding the stated splitting. At fixed x>0, A_b increases with b, so evaluating at the smaller-b maximizer proves strict monotonicity. The critical equation first gives kx_*=O(b) and x_*=O(b²), then kx_*=b/π+O(b³), which gives the stated small-b expansion.
residual_risks: The splitting is for fixed b strictly between 0 and 1; it does not give a uniform estimate at either endpoint or global iteration behavior.

value.rationale: This settles an analytic parameter-selection question for the very map the source introduced as an equilibrium-free example. The exact boundary eliminates c from that decision and tells which parameter choices inadvertently introduce a stable equilibrium. The root census, multipliers and small-b scale give information absent from the numerical slices. The value is specific to equilibria and does not rely on claims about chaos or security.
residual_risks: A complete equilibrium classification does not classify periodic orbits or establish global convergence.
